fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Trusting the Evidence of Your Senses", "body": "The conversation keeps asking why there is always some magical reason our senses must be lying. An oil rig photo shared on screen, referred to as the black swan, is offered as proof that the sea stays visible where globe curvature math predicts a 59 foot wall of water, and the refraction explanation is dismissed for lifting only the water, never the platform. Weiss offers a seasonal test too, comparing the sun's heat at a summer sunrise with a winter noon, which he says shows the sun is simply farther away. Chance urges listeners to trust their senses over the story they were told."}, {"title": "From Skeptic to Convert in Two Weeks", "body": "Weiss recalls a call with researcher Sophia Smallstorm, who told him the Earth might be flat just after he had spent half an hour banning people from his social media for suggesting it. He set out to disprove it and says he came out two weeks later convinced the spinning globe was nonsense. His first arguments are about motion: we are told we spin at 1,000 miles an hour and orbit at 66,000, he says, yet feel nothing, lakes lie like mirrors, and the three body problem that he says breaks computer models never seems to disturb the sky. Chance, who arrived through syncretism, calls himself Earth-shape agnostic."}, {"title": "Antarctica and Talk of Lands Beyond", "body": "Weiss explains his model with a puddle that grows into a pond and then a lake, until the oceans become one basin whose shoreline, Antarctica, is simply land higher than the water. He points to the Antarctic Treaty, a line at 60 degrees south past which he says nobody may explore independently, and a treaty he says cannot be questioned until 2041. Chance raises Admiral Byrd's reported land past the ice, which in his syncretic view could be the next ring out, and pictures the North Pole as the spinal cord of a living realm, while Weiss adds the Iron Republic story from magazine articles he says have vanished."}, {"title": "Reading the Sky Like a Clock", "body": "Sharing his Flat Earth clock app, Weiss describes a sky in which the sun circles every 24 hours and laps the moon about every 28 days, while the stars lap the sun once a year, so the sun keeps the days, the moon the months and the stars the seasons. He treats the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn as rings the sun moves between, explaining winter as the sun sitting farther off to the side, like a plane at the same height twenty miles away. Chance says he will use the clock to work out the time for guests in other countries."}, {"title": "Horizons, Superzooms and Sunset Tests", "body": "Asked for experiments listeners can run themselves, Weiss says our optics have outgrown the lie: a Nikon P900 superzoom can bring back a boat that seemed to sink over the horizon. He explains the effect through perspective, with the ground appearing to rise toward eye level until distant clouds merge with the horizon, and Chance compares it to the vanishing point in art. Weiss then shows a sped up drone video in which the sun never drops below the horizon but fades into the thickness of the air, and argues that a sunset is really the sun passing beyond distant clouds or land."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What if the lie about where we live matters more than the shape itself? David Weiss of DITRH joins InnerVerse to dismantle the heliocentric model and make the case that cosmological deception is the foundational inversion behind every other form of disempowerment.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: David Weiss, creator of the Flat Earth Sun Moon and Zodiac Clock app and host of the Flat Earth Podcast, walks through his case against the globe model: what he calls its mathematical impossibility, the inertia problem of spinning at a thousand miles per hour with no detectable motion, the three-body problem he says collapses heliocentric computer simulations, his view that Antarctica is the highest land on Earth and surrounds us as a basin wall, the Antarctic Treaty he says bans all independent southern exploration, the Iron Republic and stories of land beyond the ice, the flat earth clock app demonstrated live showing sun and moon circuits, how he says seasons and time zones work on a flat plane, and why he believes the drone and Nikon P900 curvature experiments tell a different story than what we were taught.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Lie Is About God, Not Geometry", "body": "Weiss opens the members hour with his one minute pitch on why the lie: convince a person they are a random accident on a random speck in an infinite godless universe, and they live in fear, turn nihilistic, and hand their power away. He asks Chance whether he believes in God, and Chance answers that he defines God as truth, which is the same thing as reality, so rejecting your own senses is its own kind of atheism. Weiss calls a created world the most physical proof of God he thinks exists."}, {"title": "An Electric Earth You Cannot Leave", "body": "The talk turns to grounding and a living Earth. Weiss says everything here, people included, is electric and magnetic in nature, that he walks barefoot year round even in winter, and that the mycelium network under the ground is the real Internet. He doubts human bodies can survive far above the Earth system. Chance takes it further, asking whether consciousness could survive outside the electromagnetic cocoon of this world, calling consciousness an extension of the land, and likening removal from it to cutting off a finger and expecting it to stay alive ten miles away."}, {"title": "How the Footage From Orbit Gets Made", "body": "Weiss builds a case that space imagery is staged. He points to wires visible on astronauts, a broadcast where the green screen glitched and everything floating glitched with it, a news segment that supposedly had only about forty five seconds of satellite time, which he notes is close to how long a zero gravity plane holds a parabola, and a crew slamming into a wall while one man caught two loose objects in a single hand. He argues Felix Baumgartner's famous curve came from a fisheye lens and a curved visor."}, {"title": "The Dome, Sky Ice, and the Missing Moon", "body": "Asked what the firmament is, Weiss grants that anything beyond Antarctica is speculation, then offers the reports he finds hard to dismiss: crews drilling blue sky ice that shrinks and disappears without leaving a puddle, and a tunnel boring machine abandoned after the wall slowly closed itself behind it. Chance hears that as an organism with a self repair function. Weiss then turns to the moon, its light that gets colder when magnified, and a new moon that nobody, even from balloons at 120,000 feet, has ever managed to see from below."}, {"title": "A Reset Roughly a Century Ago", "body": "Weiss describes interviewing Ruth, a 102 year old woman he had gone to ask about the world's fairs, who told him unprompted that her school taught the Earth was flat, and who wept when he explained the subject to her. He adds Croatian schools teaching it in the 1930s and microfilm of teachers persecuted for pushing heliocentrism, then 1918 with its masks, vaccinations and mass die off, arguing society was reset about a hundred years ago. Chance says now is the moment to start collecting data for later generations."}]
